_comment: KNOWN-GAP REPRODUCTION -- not signoff evidence. gf180-bandgap#192.
This spec exists to reproduce klayout-tools#2169 on this block, so that
erc-supply-spec.json's omission of ties[] is a measured decision with a
committed artefact behind it rather than a claim in prose.
It is erc-supply-spec.json verbatim, plus one ties[] entry declaring the
obvious gf180mcu n-well tie: well_layer Nwell 21/0, tap_layer Nplus 32/0
(gf180mcu has no distinct well-tap layer -- an n-well tap IS Comp under
Nplus inside Nwell), wired up through Metal1 to vdd. That is the
declaration a working erc.missing_tie check would need.
The measured result on this layout is not a tie verdict at all:
gate_count      10 -> 1     (the whole design collapses to one island)
erc_findings    0  -> 3, every one of them false:
erc.supply_short          vdd  / vss
erc.multiply_driven_net   vdd  / vref
erc.multiply_driven_net   vref / vss
status          not_checked -> violations, exit 3
Every declared net -- both supplies AND the block's output -- reports as
shorted to every other one, which is the signature of a single collapsed
island rather than of three real shorts.
vdd and vss are not shorted in this layout. The LVS report
(layout/lvs/reports/bandgap_top/, status 'match', 92/92 nets, 4/4 pins)
pairs them as two distinct nets, and the same klt erc run WITHOUT this
ties[] entry resolves them to two distinct islands. Registering the
well/tap layers into the connectivity graph is what merges everything.
Independent significance: klayout-tools#2169 was isolated on a routed
STANDARD-CELL design (gf180-drone-fc, FRICTION F-034, four cases). This
is a hand-drawn ANALOG layout with no standard cells, no PDN and no
filltie masters, and it collapses the same way -- so the gap is not
specific to a P&R'd cell array, and no ties[] declaration is usable in
this repo either until #2169 is fixed.
Because this report's own island model is collapsed, EVERY verdict in it
is unusable -- including its erc.missing_tie count of zero, which is
produced by the same collapse (once everything is one island, every tap
trivially reaches every net). Cite this report as evidence ABOUT THE
TOOL, never as evidence about this design.
A p-substrate tie cannot be expressed here at all, separately from
#2169: ties[].well_layer needs a DRAWN well/tub layer, and this block
sits in the native p-substrate with no LVPWELL (204/0) drawn anywhere in
the GDS. See README.md, 'What is NOT verified here'.
